examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press “What is your return policy?”. Its answer opens and the shipping answer closes. Press the same heading again to close it.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Open Privacy and security. Notification settings stays open; close either section independently.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Tab to Premium feature information. It stays focusable, and pressing it leaves its panel closed. Try “How do I update my email address?” instead.

examples.title: Collapsible
examples.caption: Open Timeline, then press it again. It stays open until you choose another heading.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Press Security to open it, then press it again. Cancel the confirmation and Security stays open; accept it and the section closes.

examples.title: Keep Mounted
examples.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply to this thread. Your draft is still there.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “pineapple”. The closed “Which fruit do you stock?” panel opens to reveal the match.

examples.title: Deep Link
examples.caption: Press Jump to the refund timeline. The closed Refunds panel opens and the browser moves to the linked paragraph.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open or close an item. Its panel animates its height.

examples.title: Expand All
examples.caption: Press Expand all or Collapse all. Open an individual week near the bottom to scroll it into view after its panel opens.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Open Billing, then Invoices inside it. The inner accordion changes without closing Billing.

examples.title: FAQ Search
examples.caption: Search for “refund” to show and open matching answers. Try “zzz” for the empty result, then clear the search to restore all questions.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Each step is an h4 with its number and a Show or Hide hint that follows its open state. Open Import the parts to see it update.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open the dialog with Enter to start on Cancel. Tab stays inside, clicking outside leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Review Changes, then Keep Editing or Discard.

examples.title: Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Cmd+Shift+H (Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Linux) to open the dialog without clicking.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open and close the dialog. It slides up and fades in, and slides down and fades out before it unmounts.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Choose Delete Workspace, then Delete. Press Escape to step back to the first question, or choose Delete Workspace to close both.

examples.title: Async Action
examples.caption: Choose Delete Project, then Delete. The first attempt fails so you can try again. While Deleting… is shown, Cancel and Escape leave the dialog open. A successful retry closes it.

examples.title: Confirm From Anywhere
examples.caption: Choose Archive Project, then Archive or Cancel. The console shows the answer.

examples.title: Confirm
examples.caption: Delete a project. Cancel or Escape keeps it; Delete removes it and focuses a neighboring row's button. Reset Projects brings the list back.

examples.title: Queued Questions
examples.caption: Choose Review Two Projects. Answer the Acme question, then the Globex question. The console shows both answers once the second one is in.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type “man”, press Down Arrow, then Enter to fill in Mango. You can also leave text that is not in the list.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try the Disabled and Read-only fields. In Disabled suggestion, type “b”: arrow keys skip Banana and a press cannot choose it.

examples.title: Clear and Trigger
examples.caption: Clear Mango, then press Show fruits to open the suggestions. The clear button disappears while the field is empty.

examples.title: Open on Focus
examples.caption: Focus Search docs to see recent searches before typing. Escape closes them; pressing the field opens them again.

examples.title: Auto Highlight
examples.caption: Type “pe” and press Enter to choose the first match. Arrow keys stop at the ends because this example disables looping.

examples.title: Inline Completion
examples.caption: Type “bl” to complete blackberry inline. Backspace removes the completion; Down Arrow fills in Blueberry. Press End to accept the text.

examples.title: Highlight Matches
examples.caption: Type “berry”. The matching letters are bold while each suggestion keeps its original spelling.

examples.title: Filter and Keywords
examples.caption: Type “bug” to find fix through its keywords. Type “re” to find labels or keywords that start with those letters.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Type “an”. Banana and Mango remain in Tropical; groups with no matches disappear.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Type “rep” and choose Replies. The icon stays out of the text put in the field.

examples.title: Items as Data
examples.caption: Open the list to see three fruit groups. Type “an” to narrow them to Banana and Mango.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Type more than 12 characters and the extra text is refused. The console shows each change and its reason.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use the buttons to open the suggestions, type Pea, clear the field or focus it from outside.

examples.title: Positioning
examples.caption: Open the suggestions. They appear above the card, aligned to its end.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Type to open the suggestions. They slide and fade in, and fade out before they unmount.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open the field to see a sheet. On touch, tap the field in its header to show the keyboard, or swipe down to close it.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Submit Apple, then choose Mango. Choosing it fills the field without submitting. Reset restores Apple.

examples.title: Search
examples.caption: Type “kotlin” and press Enter to search. Choose a suggestion to search for that text instead.

examples.title: Recent Searches
examples.caption: Focus the empty field to see Recent searches. Type “react” to search all topics, then clear the text to return to recent searches.

examples.title: Async Suggestions
examples.caption: Type “b” and wait for the city suggestions. Keep typing to replace the search; the status describes the latest results.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Type “sty” and press Enter to jump to the Styling section of this page.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Select the inset portrait to view the profile. The initials fill the same recess while the image loads.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Button, or focus it and press Enter or Space. The console logs each press.

examples.title: Pending
examples.caption: Press Save, then press it again while it saves. Nothing happens until the first action finishes.

examples.title: Pending Content
examples.caption: Press Save. Its arrow turns into a spinner while it saves.

examples.title: Handling Errors
examples.caption: Choose Save Changes. Saving always fails here: the console shows the error and the label changes to Try Again.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try clicking the button. It does nothing, and Tab skips it.

examples.title: Focusable When Disabled
examples.caption: Focus Title, then press Tab to reach Publish while it is disabled. Enter a title to enable it, then choose Publish. The console logs what was published.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Choose Get Started to jump to Installation on this page. Changelog is disabled and does not navigate.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Edit the email and choose Subscribe, or press Enter in the field. The console logs each submission, and Reset restores the original email.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose a date, then use Previous or Next to change the month. Arrow keys move through the days.

examples.title: Range
examples.caption: Choose a start date, then move to an end date to preview the range. Choose the end to finish, or press Escape to cancel the unfinished range.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose another date to add it, or choose a selected date to remove it.

examples.title: Unavailable Dates
examples.caption: Try an unavailable date, then choose an available one. Unavailable days remain focusable so their state can be heard.

examples.title: Min and Max
examples.caption: Move toward either end of the allowed dates. Keyboard navigation and month buttons stop at the limits.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try choosing a date or changing months. A disabled calendar has no available controls.

examples.title: Read Only
examples.caption: Move through dates and months. The selected value stays unchanged.

examples.title: Two Months
examples.caption: Move between October and November with arrow keys. Next advances both visible months to December and January.

examples.title: Fixed Weeks
examples.caption: Move from February to March. Both grids keep six week rows, and dates outside each month are hidden.

examples.title: Month and Year Selects
examples.caption: Choose a year and month to jump directly to a birthday, then choose the day.

examples.title: Custom Month and Year Selects
examples.caption: Choose a month or a year from the selects. The calendar follows, and the arrow keys still move between days.

examples.title: Language
examples.caption: Move through the calendar. Month names, weekday headers, and full date labels are in German, with Monday first.

examples.title: Name Formats
examples.caption: The weekday headers are narrow and the heading uses short month names: Oct – Nov 2026.

examples.title: Custom Days
examples.caption: Choose a date to see its price selected with it. Dates outside the current month have no price.

examples.title: Range Limits
examples.caption: In October 2026, choose October 15 then October 20. This example accepts 3–8 days and allows the range to span the unavailable weekend.

examples.title: Range in Progress
examples.caption: Choose a start date, then move with the arrow keys. The console logs the start and each focused date until Enter picks the end.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose a date or change the month. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Today
examples.caption: Find the marked date for today in Pacific/Kiritimati, which may differ from today in your time zone.

examples.title: Driving It from Anywhere
examples.caption: Press Go to Christmas to select December 25 and move focus there, or Today to jump back to today and select it.

examples.title: Presets
examples.caption: Choose Last 7 Days, This Month or Next 30 Days. The range is selected and the calendar shows its start.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: The table is your own markup, built from the grid's state. Navigate and select as usual.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Use Previous and Next, swipe the slides, or focus the viewport and use the arrow keys.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Scroll vertically, or use the up and down controls.

examples.title: Loop
examples.caption: Keep moving forward or backward to wrap around the slides.

examples.title: Align
examples.caption: Choose Start, Center or End, then page through the slides. Centered slides let their neighbors peek in on both sides.

examples.title: Default Page
examples.caption: Start on the chosen page, then move forward or backward.

examples.title: Indicators
examples.caption: Choose a named indicator, then use arrows, Home, and End to move between them.

examples.title: Pages
examples.caption: Move through groups of slides using the page controls.

examples.title: Thumbnails
examples.caption: Choose a thumbnail to change the gallery, or scroll either strip.

examples.title: Autoplay
examples.caption: Start or stop rotation. Hover to pause it, or move keyboard focus inside to stop it. The console logs each change and why.

examples.title: Progress
examples.caption: Move through the slides. The progress bar follows the scroll position, and the console logs the slide it rests on.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Change the page. The console logs each page and the reason for the change.

examples.title: Paging from Anywhere
examples.caption: Use the controls outside the carousel to change its page.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Change slides to see each slide and control describe its current state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click the checkbox or its label, or focus it and press Space, to accept the terms.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Click Accept terms and conditions. The field connects the label and description to the checkbox.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that checkbox is disabled. Clicking its label leaves it checked.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Tab to the checked checkbox. Space and clicks leave the setting unchanged.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Change the checkbox, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Create the account with the terms unchecked to see native validation, then accept them and try again. The console logs what was submitted, and Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Group
examples.caption: Choose several toppings. The group keeps one list of checked values.

examples.title: Parent Checkbox
examples.caption: Select all checks every topping. Uncheck one topping to put Select all into its mixed state.

examples.title: Disabled Group
examples.caption: The Backups group is disabled. In Sync folders, Select all changes the enabled folders while Desktop stays checked.

examples.title: Controlled Group
examples.caption: Choose working days, or press Select Weekdays or Clear. The console logs the group's value and the reason it changed.

examples.title: Group in a Form
examples.caption: Save with nothing checked to see the inline error. Choose a notification method and save; the console logs the submitted values.

examples.title: Table
examples.caption: Select rows individually, or use Select all in the header. The console logs how many are selected.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Check and uncheck a task. The check scales and fades in, and out before it unmounts.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Choose topics. Each checkbox renders a button that shows a check or a plus from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Order #4189, or focus it and press Enter or Space, to show the items.

examples.title: Keep Mounted
examples.caption: Open Add a delivery note, type a note, then close and reopen the panel. Your note is still there.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Leave Ingredients closed. Open your browser's Find command and search for cardamom to reveal the panel.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Open Recovery codes with Toggle or its trigger, then press Done. The console logs each change and its reason, and Done returns focus to the trigger.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open and close Release notes. The console logs when each animation finishes.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press Track parcel to open the ordered list. The summary changes from Arrives Thursday to 3 updates.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Drag across the area or along the sliders, or choose a preset. Choose HSL to write the color another way, or type one like rebeccapurple and press Enter.

examples.title: OKLCH
examples.caption: Drag the thumb right, past the painted edge, and let go. The thumb moves back to the closest color inside.

examples.title: Presets and Channel Inputs
examples.caption: Choose a preset, or use the arrow keys between them. Type 255 into the first number to set red.

examples.title: Popover
examples.caption: Press the Background swatch to open the picker, then drag to change the color.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The thumbs can't be focused or dragged.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Drag across the area and let go, or press Use Purple. The console logs each committed color and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Change the color and press Save to log the submitted value. Reset restores the orange.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type “sv” to find SvelteKit. Press Down Arrow to highlight it, then Enter to choose it.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Billing country is disabled and Shipping from is read-only. Open Shipping to: arrow keys skip Denmark, which can't be chosen.

examples.title: Clear and Trigger
examples.caption: Choose a framework, then press the clear button. The selection and text clear, focus stays in the input, and the console logs each change.

examples.title: Auto Highlight
examples.caption: Type “sw” and press Enter. The first matching country is already highlighted.

examples.title: Highlight Matches
examples.caption: Type “an”. Matching letters are marked while each country keeps its original spelling.

examples.title: Filter and Keywords
examples.caption: Type “an” and switch Filter between Contains and Starts with. Choose Fuzzy and type “swd” for Sweden, or type “deutschland” to find Germany through a keyword.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Type “chic”. Chicago remains in Americas; groups with no matches disappear.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Done. Its icon appears next to the input as well as in the list.

examples.title: Custom Items
examples.caption: Search for a person’s name or username. Choose a result to put that person’s name in the input.

examples.title: Recent Items
examples.caption: Open the empty input to see Recent. Start typing to search all countries; clear the text to return to Recent.

examples.title: Object Values
examples.caption: Choose a reviewer. The displayed selection retains the person’s object, while the form value uses their ID.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose several frameworks. Remove one with its chip button, or press Backspace in the empty input to remove the last chip.

examples.title: Select All
examples.caption: Open the list and choose a group’s select-all option. Type to narrow the matches, then use the main select-all option on those results.

examples.title: Chips That Collapse
examples.caption: Add or remove countries. Chips that no longer fit are replaced by an overflow count; the summary below lists the first two.

examples.title: Max Selected
examples.caption: Choose a third label. Other unselected labels become unavailable until you remove one.

examples.title: Create Option
examples.caption: Type a new label and choose Create. It becomes a selected chip after saving; a label longer than 20 characters shows an error.

examples.title: Custom Value
examples.caption: Type a job title that isn't suggested, then press Enter without a highlighted option or leave the field. The text becomes the value, and the console logs it.

examples.title: Input in the Popup
examples.caption: Press Country to open the search field inside the popup. Choose a country; closing the popup returns focus to the button.

examples.title: Async Search
examples.caption: Replace “the” with another movie title. The status shows the pending search, then the latest results.

examples.title: Load More
examples.caption: Open the movies and scroll or arrow to the last result. Another page loads while the existing results stay available.

examples.title: Virtualized
examples.caption: Search 10,000 items or move through them with the arrow keys. Only the nearby rows render.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Type, choose, or use the buttons. The console logs each value, query and open change with its reason.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use the buttons to drive the combobox from outside. Open and Wait logs how the list closed and what was chosen.

examples.title: Positioning
examples.caption: Pick a side and an alignment, then open the list. Check Anchor to the Box to place it against the box instead of the input.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open and close the list. The console logs when each animation finishes.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open the field to see a sheet. On touch, tap the search field in its header to bring up the keyboard, or swipe down to close it.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Submit without a country to see the inline error. Choose one and submit; the console logs the values, and Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open the list and move through it. The chevron flips while it's open, the highlighted person shows Enter, and the chosen one shows a check.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type “bil” to find Billing. Arrow keys move the highlight; Escape clears the search.

examples.title: Dialog
examples.caption: Press Search or use Cmd+K / Ctrl+K. Choose a command to run it and close the palette; the console logs what ran.

examples.title: Shortcuts
examples.caption: Press Cmd+P / Ctrl+P to run Profile, even when the search hides it. The console logs each command that runs.

examples.title: Highlight Matches
examples.caption: Type “prf” to find Profile. Matching letters are marked even when they are not next to each other.

examples.title: Filter and Keywords
examples.caption: Type “nf” with Fuzzy to find New file. Choose Words and type “zo in” for Zoom in, or type “smiley” to find Search emoji through a keyword.

examples.title: Pages
examples.caption: Choose Change theme or Switch team. Use Go back, or press Backspace in an empty search field, to return.

examples.title: Items as Data
examples.caption: Choose Change theme to open its commands. Press Cmd+I / Ctrl+I to run Open inbox from any page; the console logs what ran.

examples.title: Async Results
examples.caption: Type “login” and wait for matching issues. Replace the text to start a new search; only the latest results appear.

examples.title: Pending Actions
examples.caption: Run Deploy to production and try it again while it's pending. Sync with server fails and can be retried; the console logs each outcome.

examples.title: Virtualized
examples.caption: Search 10,000 commands or move through them with the arrow keys. Only the rows near the viewport render.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Open Change theme, search and move the highlight. The console logs each highlight, query and page change with its reason.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use the buttons to open pages, search, move the highlight and run it from outside. The console logs each command that runs.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Search for Installation and press Enter. The command follows the link to that section on this page.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click the month and type 11042026. Each part moves to the next as it fills. Press ArrowUp or ArrowDown on a part to step it.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click Birthday to focus the month, then type a date. Screen readers read the description with the input.

examples.title: Date and Time
examples.caption: Tab through the date and time. Type a P or an A in the last segment to switch between AM and PM.

examples.title: Min and Max
examples.caption: Change the year of Check-in to 2027 to see it turn invalid, then back to 2026.

examples.title: Unavailable Dates
examples.caption: Step the day of Delivery date back from Monday the 2nd to Sunday the 1st. The input turns invalid until you pick a weekday again.

examples.title: Locale
examples.caption: The same date in British English, German and Japanese. Each orders its parts its own way.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Click Start date or press Tab to reach it. Focus skips it, and the date stays November 2, 2026.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Focus Signed on and press ArrowUp or type a digit. The date stays the same.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Clear the day of Date with Backspace and choose Book to see the form stop. Fill it in and choose Book: the console logs the values. Reset brings back the defaults.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Change Due date: the console logs each whole date. Clear sets the value to null.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Choose Christmas to set the date, Edit Year to focus the year, or Clear to empty it.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: The segments here are separated by dashes in place of the locale's slashes. The order stays the locale's.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type a date and press Enter, or open the calendar and choose a day. The field formats the date when you commit it.

examples.title: Typing a Date
examples.caption: Type not a date and press Enter to mark the field invalid. Replace it with 10/18/2026 to clear the invalid state.

examples.title: Range
examples.caption: Choose October 20, then October 23. The calendar stays open after the first date and closes after the second.

examples.title: Presets
examples.caption: Open the calendar and choose Last 7 Days. Reopen it to see the selected preset.

examples.title: Min, Max and Unavailable Dates
examples.caption: Try typing 11/21/2026, past the last allowed date, then 10/17/2026, a Saturday. Both are invalid and can't be picked; 10/19/2026 is accepted.

examples.title: Language
examples.caption: Enter 3.12.2026 and press Enter. The field, format hint, and calendar use German dates.

examples.title: Clear
examples.caption: Press Clear to empty the value and focus the input. The Clear button disappears until there is a value again.

examples.title: Keep It Open Until Both Dates Are Picked
examples.caption: Choose a check-in date, then press outside the calendar. The message asks for a check-out date before the popup can be dismissed.

examples.title: Popup and Presentation
examples.caption: Open the calendar. On a small touch screen it opens as a sheet, and the console logs each open, close and month change.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Press Submit with an empty field to see the inline error, then choose a date and submit. The console logs the ISO date.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Type or choose a date. The console logs each value and the reason for the change.

examples.title: Driving It from Anywhere
examples.caption: Press Choose Christmas to set the date from outside, or Open to open the calendar.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open Share, then close it with either Close button, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

examples.title: Scrollable Content
examples.caption: Open Scrollable Content in a short window. Scroll the terms while the title and Decline/Accept buttons stay in view.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Open New Article and choose Save Draft or Publish. The console logs the submitted button's value. An empty title prevents submission.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open or press Notification Settings, then close the dialog. The console logs each change, its reason and when it finishes.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Command+J or Control+J to open New contact. The button shows the keys, and Escape returns focus to it.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open the dialog and close it. The console logs when each animation finishes; focus returns as closing starts.

examples.title: Modal
examples.caption: Choose a mode, open Notes, and try Tab or clicking the page. Check Close on outside press to compare dismissal.

examples.title: Inside a Frame
examples.caption: Open Delete Draft. The dialog and its dim cover only the frame, and Tab stays inside the dialog.

examples.title: Warn Before Closing a Dirty Form
examples.caption: Type a post, then press Escape or click outside. Keep editing returns to the field; Discard closes the dialog and clears the draft.

examples.title: Nested Dialogs
examples.caption: Open Account, then Change Password. Press Escape once to return to Account, and again to close it.

examples.title: Opening from a Menu Item
examples.caption: Open File Actions and choose Rename. Close the dialog to return focus to the File Actions button.

examples.title: Opening from Anywhere
examples.caption: Open a reminder from either unpaid invoice, or press Open from Code. The same dialog shows that invoice, and the console logs how it closed.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Edit Profile as a sheet. On a touch screen, drag it down to dismiss it, or use Cancel or Save Changes.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open View Details. The trigger's label and the description come from their state, and Close renders as a link.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open the drawer, adjust the daily goal, then Submit or Cancel. You can also press Escape, press outside, or drag the sheet toward its edge to close it.

examples.title: Scrollable Content
examples.caption: Open the long sheet and scroll its text. At the top, drag downward to move the sheet; on a keyboard, Tab reaches the controls and Escape closes it.

examples.title: Sides
examples.caption: Open a sheet from each edge. Drag it back toward that edge, press outside, or press Escape to close it.

examples.title: Snap Points
examples.caption: Open the sheet at its middle snap point. Drag it, press the handle, or Tab to the handle and use Up, Down, Home and End to try the other resting points.

examples.title: Modal
examples.caption: Open directions at the small snap point and choose another place behind the sheet. Expand it to make the sheet modal, then collapse it to use the page again.

examples.title: Nested Drawers
examples.caption: Open Account, then Change Password. The parent steps back as the child opens; Escape closes one sheet at a time.

examples.title: Outlets
examples.caption: Open Compose, then drag the sheet slowly. The inbox behind it scales and rounds with the sheet’s progress.

examples.title: Action Sheet
examples.caption: Open Photo Options and choose an action. The console logs the returned value; dismissing the sheet counts as Cancel.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Username to focus the input, then type a name.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Subscribe with an empty or invalid email, then correct it to clear the error.

examples.title: Field Sets
examples.caption: Move through the address fields. Their legend and description name the group.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Browse Files or drop a few files on the zone, then remove one. Tab to the list to move between files with the arrow keys, and press Delete to remove the focused one.

examples.title: Page-Wide Drop
examples.caption: Drag a file over this page to see the overlay, then drop it. The file joins the Attachments list; a drop on the first example's zone stays there.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Hover @hollis, or Tab to it and wait, to open Hollis Grant's profile preview. Move the pointer away or press Escape to close it.

examples.title: Positioning
examples.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then hover @ines. The card opens there and its arrow points at the link.

examples.caption: Pick a ratio, drag the selection or one of its handles, then press Crop. Tab to the selection and use the arrow keys, with Shift to move further.

examples.title: Aspect Ratio
examples.caption: Choose Square or Wide, then drag an edge. Flip mirrors the image and the crop with it.

examples.title: Frame Mode
examples.caption: Drag the image or move the zoom, then press Save Avatar. The new avatar shows beside the button.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Edit the website, then press Clear website. The text clears, focus returns to the input and the console logs the reason. Pressing https:// focuses the input too.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Shipping speed. Focus moves to the checked option, and a screen reader names the group Shipping speed.

examples.title: Slider
examples.caption: Press Volume, then use the arrow keys. The thumb moves, and a screen reader reads it as Volume.

examples.title: Switch
examples.caption: Press Email me product updates. The switch turns on.

examples.title: Wrapping a Control
examples.caption: Press Accept terms and conditions. The checkbox checks, and a double click doesn't select the text.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Comments, then hold Shift and choose New sign-ins to select the range. A click replaces the selection; Ctrl or ⌘ adds one option.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose Basil, then hold Shift and choose Pepper to select a range. Use Ctrl+A or ⌘A to select every option, then again to clear. The console logs each change.

examples.title: Selection That Follows Focus
examples.caption: Choose index.ts to replace the selection. Hold Ctrl or Cmd while choosing another file to add it; Shift selects a range.

examples.title: Manual Activation
examples.caption: Move through the options with the arrow keys. Nothing is selected until you press Space or Enter, and the console logs the choice.

examples.title: Focus on the List
examples.caption: Tab into the list and move through it with the arrow keys. Focus stays on the list, and Space or Enter chooses the highlighted option.

examples.title: Deselectable
examples.caption: Press Astro again to clear the selection, or choose another framework. The console logs each change.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Move from Apple through the list with Down Arrow. Navigation continues into the Vegetables group.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Drafts. The icon stays out of the option’s accessible name and the text used for typeahead.

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.caption: Focus M, then use Left and Right Arrow to choose a size. The list stops at its ends; XL cannot be selected.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try choosing Olive. Then press Disable the List to make every option unavailable until you enable it again.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Move focus through the frameworks. Nuxt stays selected because the list is read-only.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Choose Basil and press Order: the console logs both toppings. Reset restores Extra cheese; clearing every option makes the required list block the order.

examples.title: Object Values
examples.caption: Choose Team. The console logs the price from the selected object, not from its string ID.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Press Select All, Clear and Focus. Each button drives the same list through its controller, and the console logs the change.

examples.title: Scrollable
examples.caption: Focus the list and use the arrow keys. Options scroll into view, and the console logs the focused time zone.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Focus Remix and press Enter, or choose it with the pointer. The option is selected and its link updates the URL hash.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Open Menu and choose an item, with the pointer or the arrow keys and Enter. The menu closes and the console logs your choice.

examples.title: Submenus
examples.caption: Open Edit, then Find or Transform. Use the arrows to enter and leave each level; choosing an action closes the menu tree.

examples.title: Shortcuts
examples.caption: Open File to see shortcut hints for your platform. Choose an item to report its action; this markup example does not register global shortcuts.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Open Share and type an item’s name. The icons aren’t part of the item’s accessible name or the text typeahead matches.

examples.title: Checkboxes
examples.caption: Open View and toggle Status bar or Minimap. The menu stays open so you can change several settings, and the console logs each one.

examples.title: Radio Group
examples.caption: Open Panel and choose a position. Only one item in each group is checked, the menu stays open, and the console logs the change.

examples.title: Context Menu
examples.caption: Right-click or long-press the area, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Choose an action and the console logs it.

examples.title: Disabled Items
examples.caption: Open Document and move through its items with the arrow keys. Disabled actions remain discoverable but cannot run; Locked cannot open a menu.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open Animated, then its More tools submenu, and close them. The console logs Opening or Closing, then when the animation finishes.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Options as a sheet, enter Move to, then go back or choose a destination. You can drag downward to dismiss the sheet.

examples.title: Triggers Outside the Menu
examples.caption: Open the actions for different files. One menu shows the active row; opening from code uses the same payload and reports the closing reason.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Tab into the bar and use Left and Right to choose a menu, or point at another trigger once one is open. File has submenus, Edit has shortcuts, and View has checkboxes and an appearance choice. The console logs each one.

examples.title: Submenu
examples.caption: Open File and enter Share with the arrow key. Go back to File, then move to Edit without leaving the menubar.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Use Up and Down to choose Inbox, Drafts, or Archive. Right opens its menu in left-to-right text; Left returns to its trigger.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Read the storage meter. The label names it, and both the visible value and screen reader value report 68%.

examples.title: Bounds
examples.caption: Compare the score with the filled track. The number shows 720; the fill shows its position between 300 and 850.

examples.title: Format and Locale
examples.caption: Compare the readings. Each meter formats its own value as a unit, currency, custom text, or localized percentage.

examples.title: Value Label
examples.caption: Read API requests with a screen reader. It announces 750 of 1000 requests and 75%, while the visible value stays compact.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open each section, then use Tab or the arrow keys to move through its links.

examples.title: Link Component
examples.caption: Choose a link to update the current page without reloading the example.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Use Up and Down between the sidebar items, then open a panel beside its trigger.

examples.title: Click Only
examples.caption: Click a trigger to open it. Moving the pointer between triggers does not open another panel.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Open Components, then open Overlays or Forms. Escape closes the inner panel first.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Switch between Guides and Components to see the viewport resize and the panels slide.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open Guides to see its render state, then compare the current link and disabled trigger.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Drag the Quantity label sideways to scrub the value, or click it to focus the input. Type a number, press ArrowUp or ArrowDown, or hold a step button. The console logs the value once each change is committed.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click Tickets to focus the input, then type or step its value. Screen readers read the description with the field.

examples.title: Min and Max
examples.caption: Change Guests between 1 and 8. Type 20 and press Enter to clamp it to 8. At either bound, that direction's step button is disabled.

examples.title: Step and Large Step
examples.caption: Step Hours by 0.25. Hold Shift to move by 1, or hold Alt (Option) with an arrow key to move by 0.05. Home and End go to 0 and 24.

examples.title: Format
examples.caption: Edit Price, Discount, or Weight and leave the field to format it. Try entering 5 in Price or 25% in Discount, then use the step buttons.

examples.title: Locale
examples.caption: Edit Preis using a comma for decimals, or step Budget to see Indian digit grouping. The displayed and accepted formats follow each field's locale.

examples.title: Mouse Wheel
examples.caption: Focus Font size and scroll over it to change the value. Move focus away and scroll again; the value stays unchanged.

examples.title: Scrub Area
examples.caption: Drag the X, Y, W or H letter sideways to change that value. Hold Shift for larger steps or Alt (Option) for smaller ones. The console logs each value when the drag ends.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Hold a Servings step button. The console logs each value as it changes, then one Committed line when you let go. Clear sets the value to null, and Reset to 4 restores it.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Press Zoom In and Zoom Out to move by 100%, then Actual Size to restore 100%. Read logs the current value, and Focus moves into the field.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Change Quantity or Tip and press Save: the console logs the plain numeric values. Gift cards belongs to the same form through its form ID. Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press End in Temperature to jump to 40°C. The increment button reads Max; hover the decrement button to see its tooltip.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type a six-digit code or paste 123-456. Click a slot to edit it, use the arrow keys to move, and use your usual undo shortcut to undo a change.

examples.title: Four Digits
examples.caption: Enter four digits in PIN. Once it is full, typing another digit replaces the selected slot. Click another slot to edit it.

examples.title: Alphanumeric
examples.caption: Type letters and digits into Recovery code, or paste ab12-cd34. The hyphen is removed and the eight characters fill the slots.

examples.title: Custom Pattern
examples.caption: Try typing 12zzab into Device code. The z characters are rejected; the accepted value is 12ab, displayed as 12AB.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Verification code is marked invalid, and the error below explains why. Edit any digit to clear the error.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Enter, paste, or delete digits in One-time password. The console logs each new code and its reason.

examples.title: On Complete
examples.caption: Fill all six slots. The console logs the complete code and the change reason. Replace a digit to log it again; deleting one logs nothing.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Choose Verify with an empty or partial code to see validation. Enter all six digits and choose Verify to log the form values. Recovery code sits outside the form but submits with it. Reset clears both fields.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose a page, or use Previous and Next. The console logs each page and its reason, and the step at either end stays focusable as a button.

examples.title: Total and Page Size
examples.caption: Choose a page, then change Rows per page. The console logs each change, and a new size starts again at page 1.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Choose a page. The current page widens to say Page 3, and each arrow shows the page it goes to.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type a password, then choose Show password to reveal or hide it. Clicking the toggle keeps the caret in the field. With a keyboard, Tab to the toggle and press Space or Enter.

examples.title: New Password
examples.caption: Type a password and watch the checklist update. Try adding digits and both uppercase and lowercase letters, then toggle its visibility.

examples.title: Shown at First
examples.caption: Read the Wi-Fi password, then choose Show password to hide it. Choose it again to reveal the value.

examples.title: Caps Lock
examples.caption: Focus Password and press Caps Lock. The warning appears while Caps Lock is on. Turn it off or leave the field to hide the warning.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try to edit Password or press its toggle. Both controls are disabled and are skipped by Tab.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Choose Show recovery key to read it. Try to type in the input; its value stays unchanged.

examples.title: Controlled Visibility
examples.caption: Toggle Show password. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Choose Suggest to fill and reveal a sample value. Try Toggle, Read, Clear, and Focus to call each action from outside the field.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Enter an email and password, reveal the password, then press Enter in the field. Submission hides it again, and the console logs its length. Reset clears the form. Empty required fields block submission.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Share to open the popover, then close it with Cancel, Copy Link, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Open Edit Profile, change the name, and press Save. The popover closes and the console logs the saved name.

examples.title: Keep It Open While Editing
examples.caption: Open Add Note, type something, then press Escape or click outside. Keep Editing returns to the field; Discard closes the popover and clears the note.

examples.title: Placement
examples.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then open Delivery. Near a window edge, the popover flips or shifts to stay visible.

examples.title: Offsets
examples.caption: Change the offsets and the padding, then open Delivery. The popover moves away from the trigger and along it.

examples.title: Arrow
examples.caption: Open Help, then press Top, Right, Bottom, or Left. The popover stays open while it and its arrow move to that side.

examples.title: Anchor
examples.caption: Press the filters button. The popover lines up with the search field instead of the small button beside it.

examples.title: Modal
examples.caption: Choose a mode, open Add Comment, and try Tab or clicking the page.

examples.title: Focus
examples.caption: Open each one: Rename focuses its field, Publish focuses its Publish button, and Status leaves focus on the trigger.

examples.title: Open on Hover
examples.caption: Hover @kofi, then move into the popover and press Follow. You can also open it by pressing the trigger.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open or press Set Status, then close the popover. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Command+I or Control+I to open Invite. Press the same shortcut again, or Escape, to close it.

examples.title: Triggers Outside the Popover
examples.caption: Edit Inès Moreau or Kofi Mensah and save a new role. The owner can't be edited. Edit Newest Member opens the same editor from code, and the console logs how it closed.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open What's New, then press Got It. The console logs Opening, Open, Closing, and Closed.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Add Reminder as a sheet. Dismiss it with Cancel, Save, Escape, the dimmed area, or a downward swipe on a touch screen.

examples.title: In Place
examples.caption: Open Feedback. The panel opens above the button, inside the corner box.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open Show Updates. The trigger's label comes from its state, the title renders as an h3, and Close renders as a link.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Grid, then reload the page. The files come back in the view you chose, and the console logs each change.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Read the export bar. Its label and 60% value are available both visually and to a screen reader.

examples.title: Indeterminate
examples.caption: Read the Connecting to server bar. It shows an ongoing task without announcing a percentage.

examples.title: Changing the Value
examples.caption: Click Upload Next to add one photo, or 20%, and watch the console count them. At 100%, the button stops advancing the bar. Click Reset to start at 0%.

examples.title: Bounds
examples.caption: Compare step 3 of 5 with the fill. Because the range starts at 1, the value is halfway through the range.

examples.title: Format and Locale
examples.caption: Compare the progress readings. They show downloaded data, a precise percentage, time remaining, and a localized percentage.

examples.title: Value Label
examples.caption: Read Copying files with a screen reader. It announces 3 of 12 files and 25%, while the visible value stays compact.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Express, then use the arrow keys to move the selection between speeds.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Choose Weekly digest by its label. Each radio is also described by the line under it.

examples.title: Choice Card
examples.caption: Click anywhere on the Pro card to choose it. Arrow keys move the selection between cards too.

examples.title: Fieldset and Legend
examples.caption: Choose Yearly. The legend and the line under it describe both billing periods.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The Theme group is disabled. In Backups, Hourly is disabled, so the arrow keys move between Daily and Weekly.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Click Team, or focus Pro and press the Down arrow. Pro stays checked.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Starter, then press Choose Team. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Choose Express and press Continue. The console logs the submitted value, and Reset returns the choice to Standard.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Save without a choice to see the error. Choose SMS only and save again; the console logs the saved value.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Hover Light to preview its dot, then choose it. The dot scales in on Light and out of System.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Choose Nothing. Each radio renders a full-width button that shows a check from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose a star, then use the arrow keys to change the score.

examples.title: Half Stars
examples.caption: Choose the first half of a star. Its star fills halfway.

examples.title: Deselectable
examples.caption: Press the fourth star. The score clears.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: An average of 4.2, named Rated 4.2 out of 5.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The rating is disabled, so the stars can't be focused or pressed.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose a star, then press Clear Rating. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Press Send Review without a score to see the browser's message. Choose a star and send it again.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Drag the handle beside Files, then the one between page.tsx and Terminal.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Drag the handle between Inbox and Quarterly report, or focus it and use ArrowUp and ArrowDown.

examples.title: Handle
examples.caption: Grab the grip beside Channels, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys.

examples.title: Collapsible
examples.caption: Drag the sidebar closed to leave only its icons, or focus its handle and press Enter to collapse and restore it.

examples.title: Sizes in Pixels
examples.caption: Resize Docs. It stays between 160 and 320 pixels wide, whatever the width of the group.

examples.title: Default Layout
examples.caption: The three mail panels start at 25, 35 and 40 percent. Resize any of them.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Resize Files to log the layout and its reason. Split Evenly and Reset set the layout from outside.

examples.title: Saving on Complete
examples.caption: Drag the handle and release it, or press an arrow key. The console logs the layout once, when you let go.

examples.title: Persistence
examples.caption: Resize Outline, then reload this page to restore its saved width.

examples.title: Storage
examples.caption: Resize Messages, then reload. The width comes back in this tab, but not in a new one.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use Collapse, Expand and 240px to move Files from outside the group, and Read to log its sizes.

examples.title: Step Size
examples.caption: Focus the handle between Original and Changes. The arrow keys move it 5%, Shift with an arrow 25%, and Home and End as far as it goes.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The handle after Pinned stays fixed. Drag the one after Inbox, then check Lock layout to fix it too.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Resize Files to see both panels report their size, or collapse it to see Collapsed.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Scroll the tags with the wheel, the keyboard or the scrollbar thumb. The scrollbar shows while the pointer is over the list.

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.caption: Drag the scrollbar, or use Shift and the wheel, to scroll the palette from Sand to Ink.

examples.title: Both Axes
examples.caption: Scroll the releases down and across. The header row stays in place, and the scrollbars stop short of the corner.

examples.title: Edge Fades
examples.caption: Scroll the release notes. The top fade grows in as you leave the top, and the bottom fade shrinks away at the end.

examples.title: Native Scrollbars
examples.caption: Scroll the inbox with the browser's own scrollbar. The scroll area still tracks its edges and state.

examples.title: When Scrollbars Show
examples.caption: Hover and scroll each list to compare. The auto and always scrollbars show from the start; hover waits for the pointer and scroll for scrolling.

examples.title: Hide Delay
examples.caption: Scroll each list and stop. The scrollbar on the left hides at once; the one on the right waits 2000 milliseconds.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Press Jump to the End, then Back to Top. The console logs each end of the list as the view reaches it.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Scroll the releases. The hint under the list reads the root's state, changes once you leave the top, and disappears at the end.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Grid, then use the arrow keys to move between views. The label above names the control, as in any field.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Choose Bottom, then press the Up arrow. The indicator follows down the column.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The Theme control is disabled. In Billing period, Lifetime is disabled, so the arrow keys move between Monthly and Yearly.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Day, then press Show Month. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Choose Dark and Compact, then press Save. The console logs both values, and Reset returns each control to its default.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open Role and choose Editor. The list closes and the trigger shows your choice.

examples.title: Items as Data
examples.caption: Open Plan to see the options, separator, and Contact sales group. Education is disabled; choose Enterprise to update the value.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Open Font and choose from Sans serif, Serif or Monospace. Each group has a label that screen readers announce.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Center or End. Both the label and the icon in the trigger update to match the selected item.

examples.title: Typeahead
examples.caption: Focus Country and type “sw” to select Sweden without opening the list. Open it and type “g” to highlight Germany, then press Enter.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Billing country is disabled and Shipping from is read-only. Open Shipping to and press the arrow keys: the highlight skips Denmark, which can't be chosen.

examples.title: Clear Button
examples.caption: Press the clear button. The trigger shows Unassigned, focus returns to it, and the console logs null. Choose someone to bring the button back.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose several languages, then choose one again to remove it. The list stays open, and the console logs the array.

examples.title: Select All
examples.caption: Open Regions and press Select all. Press it again to clear the selection, then choose one region to see the mixed state.

examples.title: Search with Groups
examples.caption: Open Country and type “ja”. Only Asia Pacific and Japan remain. Try “zz” to see the empty message, then clear the search to show every country.

examples.title: Async Search
examples.caption: Open Country and type “an”. Results arrive after a short delay. Clear the search and move or scroll to the last result to load another page.

examples.title: Object Values
examples.caption: Inès starts selected even though the initial value is a copy of her item. Choose another assignee; the console logs the ID the form submits.

examples.title: Virtualized
examples.caption: Open Item and press End to reach Item 10000, then Home to return to the beginning. Scroll through the list; only nearby rows render.

examples.title: Align Item with Trigger
examples.caption: Open Priority: Medium sits over the trigger. Close it, uncheck Align item with trigger, and open it again to compare placement.

examples.title: Scrollable
examples.caption: Open Time zone and move down with the arrow keys. The list scrolls to keep the highlighted option visible.

examples.title: Invalid
examples.caption: Press Continue without choosing a shipping method to show the error. Choose one and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Choose a country and some topics, change Frequency, then press Save; the console logs all three fields. Reset restores the initial choices.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Status to show the bottom sheet. Choose an option to close it, or drag down to dismiss it without changing the value.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Read the profile with a screen reader. It announces a separator between Hollis Grant's name and email and the bio below.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Read across Privacy, Terms and Cookies. A screen reader announces a vertical separator between each link.

examples.title: Stacked Content
examples.caption: Compare the lines with the stats. Each one runs the full height of Projects, Followers and Following.

examples.title: Rows
examples.caption: Read the plan details with a screen reader. It announces a separator between Plan, Seats and Renews.

examples.title: Decorative
examples.caption: Read from Sign In with Passkey to Email Me a Link with a screen reader. It reads “or” and skips the lines.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Drag the thumb, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to adjust Volume.

examples.title: Range
examples.caption: Move either end of Price. The thumbs stay in order.

examples.title: Multiple Thumbs
examples.caption: Adjust Low, Medium and High independently, without moving one past another.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Drag up or down, or use the arrow keys, to adjust Bass and Treble.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click the Volume label to focus the thumb, then use the arrow keys to change the value.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Brightness keeps its value, but can't be focused or dragged.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Drag either Temperature thumb to log the range and its reason. Reset sets the value from outside.

examples.title: Step and Bounds
examples.caption: Move Year in steps of five, and Opacity in steps of 0.05.

examples.title: Large Step
examples.caption: Focus Zoom and press an arrow key to move 1%, then Page Up, Page Down or Shift with an arrow key to move 25%.

examples.title: Distance Between Thumbs
examples.caption: Move either end of Opening hours. The thumbs stay at least four hours apart.

examples.title: Format and Locale
examples.caption: Adjust Budget, Opacity, Weight, Duration and Preis to compare currency, a percentage, a unit, a custom function and German formatting.

examples.title: Saving on Commit
examples.caption: Drag Brightness and release it, or press an arrow key. The console logs the value once, when you let go.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use Mute, Louder and Focus to operate Volume from outside the slider. The console logs each change with the imperative reason, and Read logs the value.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Adjust the filters and press Save to log the submitted values. Distance sits outside the form and joins it by id. Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Focus or drag the Brightness thumb to show its value above it.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Airplane mode, or focus the switch and press Space, to turn it on and off.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Click Weekly digest. The field connects the label and description to the switch.

examples.title: Choice Card
examples.caption: Click anywhere on the Public profile card to turn it on. Each card's switch keeps its own value.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that switch is disabled. Clicking it leaves it on, and Tab skips it.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Tab to Encrypt backups. Space and clicks leave it on.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Turn Wi-Fi off, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Turn on Product updates and press Save. The console logs the submitted values, and Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Continue with the switch off to see the error. Turn on Two-factor authentication and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

examples.title: Saving on Toggle
examples.caption: Turn on Automatic backups. The thumb shows a spinner while it saves, then the switch turns on.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Turn on Dark mode. The thumb renders a sun or a moon from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Password to show its panel. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between the tabs.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Focus General, then press Down Arrow to choose Security. Up Arrow moves back through the vertical list.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Use the arrow keys to reach Reports. It can receive focus, but pressing it leaves the current panel selected.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Replies. Its directional icon mirrors when the surrounding page uses right-to-left text.

examples.title: Manual Activation
examples.caption: Focus Preview, then press Right Arrow. Code receives focus; press Enter or Space to show its panel. Tab then moves into the Source field.

examples.title: Loop
examples.caption: Focus Year and press Right Arrow. Focus stays at the end because looping is off.

examples.title: Indicator
examples.caption: Choose Podcasts, then choose Vertical. The same indicator measures and follows the selected tab in either layout.

examples.title: Keep Mounted
examples.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply. Your draft is still there.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “restocking fee”. Returns opens to reveal the match.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Move between Overview, Activity and Settings. The panels slide in the direction you moved.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Drafts, then press Show Sent Mail. The console logs each new value with its reason.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Choose Activity. Its panel opens and the URL hash changes. Modified clicks keep the link’s usual browser behavior.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Each tab renders its own button with an unread count after the label. Choose Unread to see who wrote to you.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Message to focus the textarea, then type. Press Enter to start a new line.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click Feedback to focus the textarea. A screen reader reads the description with the field.

examples.title: Auto Resize
examples.caption: Type several lines in Notes. The textarea grows with each line until it reaches its maximum height, then scrolls. Delete the lines and it shrinks back.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Edit Bio and watch the character count under it. The textarea stops accepting text at 160 characters.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Type a message and press Send Message. The console logs it and the textarea clears. Pressing Send Message while it's empty is blocked.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try to edit Reply or reach it with Tab. The disabled textarea keeps its value but can't be changed.

examples.title: Invalid
examples.caption: Focus Review. The textarea is marked invalid, and the error below says how long the review should be.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click the hour and type 230, then P. Press ArrowUp or ArrowDown on a part to step it.

examples.title: Clock and Seconds
examples.caption: The same evening time on a 12-hour clock, a 24-hour clock and with seconds. All three submit 24-hour values.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Tab into the activity, then use Up and Down to move between events. Home and End jump to the first and last.

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.caption: Tab into the roadmap and press Right to reach Launch. Right again stays there.

examples.title: Status
examples.caption: Tab into the order status. Focus starts on Shipped, the current step. Move away, then choose Go to Current Step.

examples.title: Details
examples.caption: Tab to What Changed under Version 2.4 and press Enter. Shift+Tab back to the event, then press Down for Version 2.3.

examples.title: Feed
examples.caption: Tab into the updates and press Page Down. Choose Load More: the feed is busy until three more updates arrive. The console logs each load.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Create Event. Choose Undo, swipe the toast away, or wait for it to close. Undo logs Event removed.

examples.title: Types
examples.caption: Choose a type. Each toast shows its type's icon, and Loading turns into Photos uploaded when it finishes.

examples.title: Position
examples.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then press Create Event and look for the toast at that edge of the page.

examples.title: Action and Cancel
examples.caption: Press Archive Message, then choose Undo or Dismiss, swipe the toast away, or let it time out. The console logs why it closed.

examples.title: Link
examples.caption: Press Send Invoice, then follow View in the toast.

examples.title: Promise
examples.caption: Press Save Changes to see Saving changes become Changes saved. Press it again for the error, then choose Retry.

examples.title: Stacking
examples.caption: Press Add Toast a few times, then hover the stack to expand it. Past four toasts, the rest wait their turn. Check Always expanded to keep it open.

examples.title: Duration
examples.caption: Press each button. Hover a toast to pause its timer. The session toast stays until you press Got It.

examples.title: Update and Dismiss
examples.caption: Press Upload Report and watch one toast count up to Report uploaded. Cancel Upload closes it early, and Dismiss All clears every toast.

examples.title: Async Action
examples.caption: Press Delete File, then Undo. The button shows Restoring… until the restore finishes, then the toast closes.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Send Message, then Alt+T (Option+T on a Mac) to focus the toast. Press Escape to dismiss it, or Alt+T again to go back.

examples.title: Overlay Host and Confirm
examples.caption: Press Delete on a project and confirm. The row goes away and a toast says so. Reset Projects brings them back.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press New Message to show a toast with Hollis Grant's initials. Choose Reply or close it.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press the star beside Q3 Roadmap, or focus it and press Enter or Space. It fills in while pressed, and its accessible name stays Star.

examples.title: Group
examples.caption: Press Bold and Italic to keep both pressed. Left and Right move focus without changing either.

examples.title: Single Selection
examples.caption: Press Align center to replace Align start, then press Align center again. One alignment always stays pressed.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press Favorite. The heart renders filled or empty from the toggle's pressed state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type @ and choose a person with the arrow keys and Enter. Remove a token with Backspace, or press its remove button.

examples.title: Prompt Input
examples.caption: Type @ for files or / at the start for skills. For /search, enter a query and press Enter to insert the command. Press Enter again to send, and the console logs the message.

examples.title: Deleting Tokens
examples.caption: Choose a Backspace behavior, click just after routes.ts, and press Backspace. Undo to try another behavior.

examples.title: Codec
examples.caption: Edit the message. The console logs it in the custom format, with each mention as <@id>.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Press Submit to log the prompt's serialized value. Try Disabled and Read-only, then Reset.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Type, add a file with @, or remove a token. The console logs the value and the reason for each change.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Attach a file and watch it load. Show the first token's full path or remove it, then use Undo or Clear.

examples.title: Submit Shortcut
examples.caption: Write a message. Enter adds a line; Command+Enter on a Mac or Control+Enter elsewhere sends it to the console.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Tab into the toolbar, then use Left and Right to move between Bold, Italic, Underline and Insert link. Press Space to toggle the focused style. The console logs each change.

examples.title: Toggle Groups
examples.caption: Arrow from the alignment group to the list group, then press Space on Align center or Numbered list. The console logs each choice.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Move through Cut, Copy and Paste into History with the arrow keys. Undo and Redo stay focusable but do nothing.

examples.title: Menus
examples.caption: Focus Share and press Down, then choose Email or Copy Link. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to Share.

examples.title: Selects
examples.caption: Open Zoom and choose a value, or step it with Zoom out and Zoom in. Each button turns off at the end of the range.

examples.title: Fields
examples.caption: Move into Font size and press Up or Down to change it. In Find, type a word, then move the caret to an edge before that arrow leaves the field.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Arrow to Files Changed and press Enter. The console logs the page it opened.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Use Up and Down to move between the tools and Delete. Space picks the focused tool.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Arrow from Reply to Archive, which is disabled but focusable. Delete is skipped. Only Reply logs a press.

examples.title: Loop
examples.caption: Focus Last and press Right. Focus stays there; Home still moves to First.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Type in Notes, then press Alt+F10 or choose Focus Toolbar. Press a toolbar button and the console logs it.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: The tooltip starts open. Hover the button or reach it with Tab to show it again, and Escape closes it while focus stays on the button.

examples.title: Side
examples.caption: Hover Top, Left, Right and Bottom. Each tooltip opens on that side of its button, or flips into the middle when there isn't room.

examples.title: Anchor
examples.caption: Hover the help button. The tooltip opens below the Webhook URL field and lines up with its start, not with the button.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Hover Save or Share to read its shortcut, then press the button or the keys. The console logs Saved or Shared.

examples.title: Disabled Buttons
examples.caption: Hover or focus Publish to learn what's missing. Type a title, and Publish works and its tooltip goes away.

examples.title: Touch
examples.caption: Press the info button to open the tip, including on a touch screen. Press it again or anywhere else to close it.

examples.title: Keep Open on Press
examples.caption: Hover the copy button and press it. The tooltip stays open and changes to Copied.

examples.title: Truncated Text
examples.caption: Hover or focus each file. Only names that are cut off open a tooltip.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open, or hover Export. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Shared
examples.caption: Move along Bold, Italic and Underline. One tooltip follows the pointer and shows each button's label.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Hover Archive, then move away. The tooltip grows out of the button and fades, and the console logs Opening, Open, Closing and Closed.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Hover Changelog. The trigger renders as a link, and its tooltip says where it goes.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Expand components to see its files. Use the arrow keys to move between rows and open or close branches.

examples.title: File Paths
examples.caption: Arrow down to package.json, then press Enter. It shows a spinner while it opens, then the console logs Opened package.json.

examples.title: Multiple Selection
examples.caption: Cmd-click or Ctrl-click Archive to add it to the selection. Shift-click or Shift+Arrow extends a range, and the console logs what's selected.

examples.title: Checkboxes
examples.caption: Press Space on Vue, then on Frontend. Frontend is mixed while only some of its items are checked, and the console logs the trunk strategy's values.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Choose Dialog. The current-page marker moves to it, and you stay on this docs page.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Arrow through Enterprise while Focusable when disabled is on. Turn it off and the same arrow keys skip disabled items.

examples.title: Loading Children
examples.caption: Expand users to load its files. Archive fails on its first attempt and shows a retry icon; expand it again to load it.

examples.title: Virtualized
examples.caption: Expand folders or press End to focus Folder 100. The tree has 10,100 items, but only nearby rows render.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Use your browser's Find command to look for Phobos, a moon of Mars. The matching branches open to reveal it.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Press Find Two-Factor to open Account and Security, then select and focus Two-factor authentication. Collapse All closes every branch.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Type @, narrow the list with a name, and press Enter to insert the highlighted person.

examples.title: Triggers as Data
examples.caption: Type @ for people, / at the start for commands, or # to load channels.

examples.title: Commands with Arguments
examples.caption: Type /status, then press Tab to choose a status and an optional time, and Enter to finish. Choose /away to send it at once. The console logs each command.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Type / to open the commands, then type re to narrow them. Each icon sits before its name, and filtering ignores it.

examples.title: Loading Items
examples.caption: Type # and a channel name. The list says it's loading, and older results fade while newer ones load.

examples.title: Custom Items
examples.caption: Type @ and the start of a first name to insert it, or choose Notify everyone here to insert @here. Deactivated people can't be chosen.

examples.title: Input
examples.caption: Type @ in the empty task. Nothing is highlighted until you press ArrowDown, then Enter assigns the person.

examples.title: Positioning
examples.caption: Type @ in the comment. The list opens above the field, lined up with its label.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Type @ and a name, press Escape, then Control+J to reopen the list. The console logs each callback with its reason.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Press Mention and choose a person. The console logs why the list closed. Insert Date adds today's date at the caret.

examples.title: Any Editor
examples.caption: Type @ in the notes, a textarea connected through an editor adapter, and choose a person.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Use the arrow keys to move between requests. Press Right to move into a row's cells, where each bar reads out when its request starts and how long it takes.

examples.title: Nested Spans
examples.caption: Expand payments.charge with Right, then press Enter on gateway.capture. The console logs the selected span. Collapse All closes every span.

examples.title: Zoom
examples.caption: Press Zoom In twice. The axis shows smaller steps, and the metrics span stretches past the edges.

examples.title: Large Traces
examples.caption: Press End to focus job 2000, or Page Down to move a page at a time. The trace has 10,000 spans, but only nearby rows render.
